chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What do people narrate, that prayer in congregation is superior to the prayer of a man alone by twenty-five prayers?' He said, 'They are truthful.' I said, 'When two men are in congregation?' He said, 'Yes, and the man stands to the right of the Imam.'

key_terms.بِخَمْسٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ: By twenty-five (referring to the multiplier of reward)
key_terms.عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلْإِمَامِ: To the right of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of people required for a valid congregational prayer (jama'ah) in Shia Islam, and what is its spiritual merit compared to individual prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the widely held view that congregational prayer holds a merit twenty-five times greater than individual prayer, a metric rooted in early Shia juristic consensus. He further clarifies the minimal threshold for 'congregation' (jama'ah), establishing that even two men suffice, with the follower positioned to the right of the Imam, thereby emphasizing the structural simplicity and accessibility of communal worship in Shia fiqh. This hadith serves as a foundational text for the ruling that the minimum quorum for valid congregational prayer is two, excluding the Imam.
